name: Haryana

nextRevision.basis: The 9 April 2026 notification leaves adjustments to the Code on Wages (Haryana) Rules, which are still in draft; draft rule 5 revises the VDA before 1 April and 1 October each year. Before 2026 Haryana revised every 1 January and 1 July, a cycle the April 2026 notification ended. No final rules and no VDA order were on the Department's listing on 17 October 2026, so no revision is treated as overdue.

sources.title: Revised basic minimum rates of wages for all employments, with effect from 1 April 2026
sources.legalBasis: Section 8(3), Code on Wages, 2019. Haryana Government Gazette (Extraordinary) No. 51-2026/Ext., 9 April 2026. Replaces the basic rates of notification 3/42/83-3 Lab dated 21 October 2015.

sources.title: Implementation of the notification dated 9 April 2026 fixing minimum rates of wages
sources.legalBasis: Directs field officers to enforce the 9 April 2026 notification in all establishments, including petty establishments, while CWP-PIL-255 of 2026 (Court on its own motion v. State of Haryana) is pending in the Punjab and Haryana High Court.

sources.title: List of 50 scheduled employments (Minimum Wages Act notification of 21 October 2015; its rates are superseded)
sources.legalBasis: Minimum Wages Act, 1948, section 5(2). Haryana Government Gazette (Extraordinary) No. 185-2015/Ext., 21 October 2015, pages 2549-2556, in Hindi and English.

sources.title: Increase in minimum wages from 1 July 2025 on the consumer price index, including brick kilns
sources.legalBasis: A rise of 0.23 per cent from 1 July 2025 on the basic rates of notification 3/42/83-3 Lab. of 21 October 2015 (Minimum Wages Act, 1948), the consumer price index having moved from 3438.5 to 3446.3.

tables.title: All employments
tables.appliesTo: Every employment in Haryana: establishments, factories, employees, workers and contract labour as the Code on Wages, 2019 defines them. Brick kilns are to be notified separately. Trainees get 75% of their category's rate for up to a year, but not less than the unskilled rate.

zones.name: All of Haryana
zones.areas: One rate for the whole state.

tables.vdaNote: The notification fixes all-inclusive basic rates that an employer may not split into allowances. Rises in the consumer price index are to be passed on in full as the Code on Wages (Haryana) Rules, 2026 prescribe; no dearness allowance has been notified on these rates yet.

groups.note: Chunai wala, mistri, coalman and jalai wala: ₹13,051.71 a month. These are the last brick-kiln rates the labour department published, from 1 July 2025, on the 2015 notification. The April 2026 notification says brick-kiln rates will be notified separately, and none has been yet.

verification: 2026-10-17: The Labour Department's 'News & Notifications' listing (hrylabour.gov.in, cat_id 46) links 'Revise Basic Minimum wages Notification dated 09-04-2026 w.e.f. 01-04-2026 in the State of Haryana' (storage.hrylabour.gov.in ... 1775725409.pdf). It is the Haryana Government Gazette (Extraordinary) No. 51-2026/Ext. of 9 April 2026, notification No. 2/25/26-2 Lab., with a text layer; figures read from it: per month 15220.71 / 16780.74 / 18500.81 / 19425.85, per day 585.41 / 645.41 / 711.56 / 747.14.

2026-10-17: The stated daily rates are the monthly rate divided by 26 and cut (not rounded) to the paisa: 18500.81 / 26 = 711.5696 is printed 711.56, 19425.85 / 26 = 747.148 is printed 747.14. The notification's note 7 sets the 26-day divisor. The printed figures are used.

2026-10-17: The notification has four categories only (unskilled, semi-skilled, skilled, highly skilled). The 2015 scheme's A/B grades and clerical, driver and security-guard rows (Labour Commissioner's letter 5377-522 of 22 February 2024, rates from 1 January 2024: unskilled 10924.24) are not carried over; the reviewer should confirm that clerical and other staff now fall in these four categories.

2026-10-17: Order No. 25744-860 of 5 October 2026 (Labour Commissioner, scanned, read from the page image) directs enforcement in all establishments including petty establishments, because CWP-PIL-255 of 2026 alleges the notification is not being implemented; the High Court hearing is listed for 28 October 2026.

2026-10-17: OPEN QUESTION for the reviewer: no VDA or dearness revision on the April 2026 rates was found on the listing (checked back to 2024). The draft Code on Wages (Haryana) Rules, 2026 (notification 02/08/2021-2Lab., 4 May 2026) say the VDA is revised before 1 April and 1 October; until the rules are final, whether a revision was due on 1 October 2026 is uncertain. nextRevision.expected is set to 1 October 2026 on that draft rule.

2026-10-17: Next revision. Note 1 of the 9 April 2026 notification (Gazette Ext. No. 51-2026, p. 409): full neutralisation of the consumer price index, 'the adjustment in wages shall be made further as prescribed in Code on Wages Rules, 2026'. The draft rules (No. 02/08/2021-2Lab., Gazette Ext. No. 66-2026, 4 May 2026, rule 5) compute the VDA before 1 April and 1 October. Not final; nothing newer on the listing. Expected set to 2027-04-01 with no missed dates.

2026-10-17: Clerical and other staff. The notification has four categories and lists no occupations. Schedule A of the draft wage rules (4 May 2026, pp. 771-790) places clerks, typists, data entry operators, store keepers, time keepers and motor vehicle drivers under Skilled, accountants and armed guards under Highly skilled, and peons, helpers, loaders, sweepers and cleaners under Unskilled (watchman appears under both Unskilled and Semi-skilled). Draft, not binding.

2026-10-17: the 9 April 2026 notification fixes rates 'in respect of all the employments' and lists none; its one exception: 'The rate of wages applicable on brick kilns will be notified separately.' The last list of employments is the Schedule of notification 3/42/83-3 Lab. of 21 October 2015 (Gazette Ext. 185-2015, pages 2553-2554, English, read by eye): 50 employments, including 40 Agriculture, 48 Brick Kiln, 49 Domestic worker and 50 Safai Karamchari. The page lists 48 of them as names to find one's work by, leaving out brick kilns and safai karamcharis (struck from the schedule by the High Court in CWP 25328 of 2015, as the Labour Commissioner's letter 5377-522 of 22 February 2024 records).

2026-10-17: no brick-kiln notification under the Code on Wages on hrylabour.gov.in (listings cat_id 46 to August 2024 and its archive, 51 and 70, searched for brick, kiln, bhatta, wage, minimum). The last brick-kiln figures the department published are in letter 5377-522 of 22 February 2024 (piece rates from 1 January 2024, on the 2015 notification); no later CPI letter is online, so the page shows no brick-kiln figures. The Haryana e-Gazette search needs a captcha and was not searched.

2026-10-17: hrylabour.gov.in has a 'Minimum Wages' listing (cat_id=53) that carries every half-yearly CPI letter: 1 July 2024 (IR-2/2024/25852-26005), 1 January 2025 (IR-2/2025/11047-89) and 1 July 2025 (IR-2/2025/28373-498 of 30 October 2025, 1761820413.pdf, sha256 0f90a186...). The last, read by eye at 110 dpi: CPI 3438.5 to 3446.3, 0.23 per cent; page 3, brick kilns from 1 July 2025: pathera 642.37 per thousand bricks and 721.67 per thousand tiles; bharai wala (a) 289.03 up to 400 m plus 25.63 for each further 100 m, by donkey or mule only; (b) 237.61 up to 1000 m by tempo, animal-drawn rehri or other mechanical vehicle, plus 25.63 for each further 500 m; keri wala 51.33; nikasi wala 211.94; chunai wala and mistri/coalman/jalai wala 13051.71 a month. Each figure is the 2015 basic times the cumulative CPI rises. No letter for 1 January 2026: the Code on Wages took effect on 21 November 2025 and the 9 April 2026 notification replaced the 2015 rates from 1 April 2026, leaving brick kilns to be notified separately. The Haryana e-Gazette (searched past its captcha) holds no brick-kiln notification under the Code.
